title: Integral scalar extension preserves bounded constructible integral complexes
statement: Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\Ql$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, with $\ell\neq p$, and let $Y$ be a scheme. For every $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the integral scalar extension $K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] lies in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_L)$. Hence integral scalar extension restricts to an $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_L)$.

source.place: last paragraph (the functor $-\otimes_EL:D^b_c(Y,E)\to D^b_c(Y,L)$ is defined on integral representatives, which presupposes this); also asserted in dag node lem-coef-integral-finite-extension ('This exact functor preserves the integral bounded constructible categories')

proof.text: Write $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, $k_E=R/(\varpi_E)$ and $k_L=S/(\varpi_L)$, with completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_Y$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] the residue fields are finite and both valuation rings are DVRs. The maps of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] induce $k_E\to k_L$: $\varpi_E\in\varpi_L S$. This is a unital map of fields, hence injective. Since $k_L$ is a finite set, successively adjoining a vector outside the span of the vectors already chosen terminates and gives a finite $k_E$-basis, say of length $d$. By [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] choose $r\le s$ bounding the cohomology of all reductions of $K$, in particular $K_1=K\otimes^L_R k_E$; its cohomology sheaves are constructible. Only this first reduction and its bound will be used in the finite-level argument.

source.place: last paragraph; elementary residue-field preparation using the coefficient DVR theorem

proof.text:
Choose one K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms as in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For $m\ge1$ put $B_m=S/(\varpi_L^m)$ and $M_m=P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(B_m)_Y$, with the strict quotient transition maps. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] these complexes compute $K\otimes^L_R B_m$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $M_m$ is K-flat with flat terms over $(B_m)_Y$. Consequently, for $m\ge n$, derived reduction of $M_m$ to $B_n$ is computed by its ordinary tensor, and the map
$$(P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(B_m)_Y)\otimes_{(B_m)_Y}(B_n)_Y\longrightarrow P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(B_n)_Y$$
is an isomorphism of complexes. Its local tensor formula is $(p\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto p\otimes bc$, with inverse $p\otimes c\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes c$; balancing makes the maps inverse. The maps commute with differentials, and for $m\ge n\ge a$ both composites send $(p\otimes b)\otimes c\otimes z$ to $p\otimes bcz$. Thus the adjoints of the specified transition maps are these isomorphisms and satisfy the quotient cocycle. The strict system is a normalized DVR tower in the sense of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]; this establishes normalization rather than assuming it.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); explicit balanced tensor comparison and quotient cocycle

proof.text: First treat the common layer $Q=P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(k_L)_Y$. Put $P_1=P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(k_E)_Y$, representing $K_1$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $P_1$ is K-flat over $(k_E)_Y$, so $P_1\otimes_{(k_E)_Y}(k_L)_Y$ computes $K_1\otimes^L_{k_E} k_L$. The coefficient map $\widehat R_Y\to(k_L)_Y$ factors through $(k_E)_Y$ by the residue map of step 1. The balanced maps $(p\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes ab$ and $p\otimes b\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes b$ are inverse chain maps identifying this complex with $Q$. The chosen $k_E$-basis identifies $(k_L)_Y$ with $(k_E)_Y^{\oplus d}$, so tensoring with it is a finite direct sum of the identity functor. It is exact, and $\mathcal H^i(Q)=\mathcal H^i(K_1)\otimes_{k_E}k_L$; this also follows by computing cycles and boundaries in the finite direct sum. For the finitely many degrees $r\le i\le s$, take a common finite refinement of their constructible stratifications: its members are intersections of the locally closed constructible members, so remain locally closed constructible and partition $Y$. Pullback to such a stratum is exact and commutes with constants and tensor, by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. On a cover trivializing $\mathcal H^i(K_1)$ to the constant sheaf of a finite $k_E$-module $V$, the displayed cohomology of $Q$ is the constant sheaf of $V\otimes_{k_E}k_L$, with its actual $k_L$-action. For clarity, inverse image takes each constant coefficient ring to the same constant ring: the constant set sheaf is the copower of the terminal sheaf indexed by the ring, and the cited inverse-image theorem preserves both terminal objects and colimits; addition and multiplication are transported because it preserves finite products. Thus module pullback here is the exact inverse image, not tensor along an unknown ring comparison. The constant tensor identification is induced by $v\otimes c\mapsto v\otimes c$ in the sheafified tensor presentation. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] justifies the constant tensor and cohomology calculation. This module is finite, as a quotient of the finite set $V\otimes_{k_E}k_E^{\oplus d}\cong V^{\oplus d}$. Therefore $Q$ has constructible $k_L$-cohomology and support in $[r,s]$. For each $m$, regard $Q$ as a $(B_m)_Y$-complex via $B_m\to k_L$; the same constant models show constructibility as $B_m$-modules, with the same support.

source.place: Tag 0G7E; elementary finite free residue-field extension, with exact inverse image and exact constant sheafification

proof.text:
Fix $m$. Filter the $B_m$-module $B_m$ by the ideals $J_j=\varpi_L^j S/\varpi_L^m S$ for $0\le j\le m$. Thus $J_0=B_m$, $J_m=0$, and multiplication by $\varpi_L^j$ induces a $B_m$-linear isomorphism $k_L\cong J_j/J_{j+1}$ for $j<m$. It is surjective by the definition of $J_j$; its kernel is $(\varpi_L)$ since $S$ is a domain and $\varpi_L^m S\subseteq\varpi_L^{j+1}S$, so cancellation of $\varpi_L^j$ reduces the kernel assertion to membership in $\varpi_L S$ [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. In particular each $J_j/J_{j+1}$ is a finite set. Descending induction using the fibers of $J_j\to J_j/J_{j+1}$ (each a coset of $J_{j+1}$) shows that $J_j$ is finite, starting with $J_m=0$. Thus $B_m=J_0$ is indeed a finite commutative ring, as required for the constructible-subcategory theorem below. Exact constant sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] gives short exact coefficient sheaf sequences $0\to(J_{j+1})_Y\to(J_j)_Y\to(k_L)_Y\to0$. They are sequences of $\widehat R_Y$-modules as well, through the compatible coefficient maps. Because each $P^q$ is flat, tensoring produces degreewise short exact sequences of $B_m$-complexes
$$0\to P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(J_{j+1})_Y\to P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(J_j)_Y\to Q\to0.$$
They yield distinguished triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Descending induction from $j=m$ now proves that every middle complex has constructible cohomology and support in $[r,s]$: the base is the zero complex; the induction step uses the constructible layer $Q$ from step 3 and extension closure [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] for the finite ring $B_m$. For a degree $i$ outside $[r,s]$, the two outer cohomology objects vanish, so the middle one vanishes by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. At $j=0$ this complex is $M_m$. The interval never changes during the induction and is independent of $m$; no flatness of $B_m$ over $A_{E,m}$, no finite Tor hypothesis and no Noetherian hypothesis on $Y$ were used.

proof.text: Let $N=K\otimes_R S$ be the object defined by [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. It is the fixed cone $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ of the strict tower $\operatorname{Res}^L_mM_m$, and is a derived limit of that tower by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. Step 2 verified precisely the normalized-tower hypothesis of [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity], with the DVR $S$ and quotient rings $B_m=A_{L,m}$. Apply that theorem to obtain compatible isomorphisms $N\otimes^L_S B_m\cong M_m$ and derived completeness of $N$. This is the same derived limit as the normalized-tower theorem: the strict tower theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] computes total derived inverse limit by its Roos triangle. Countable products of completed-coefficient module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], so [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] identifies the derived products in that triangle with the termwise products used here. To make the comparison explicit, take the strict tower resolution $X_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ used by the strict-tower theorem, where $X_m=\operatorname{Res}^L_mM_m$. Its maps are termwise quasi-isomorphisms and commute with the transitions. Exact countable products imply that $\prod_mX_m\to\prod_mI_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism: cohomology of these products is the product of the cohomologies by [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core]. The commuting square with $1-s$ therefore induces a quasi-isomorphism of the shifted mapping-cone complexes. On each evaluation it commutes with projection to the corresponding tower member, since the square came from a strict tower map. The Roos model of the strict-tower theorem is consequently identified with the fixed cone defining $N$, with its evaluations. This supplies the comparison needed for the canonical counit isomorphisms of the effectivity theorem, without asserting uniqueness of arbitrary cone maps. The finite-level statement of step 4 therefore supplies constructibility and the single interval $[r,s]$ for all derived reductions of $N$. These are exactly the conditions of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] for $L$, so $N\in D^b_c(Y,S)$. Finally the ambient functor is $R$-linear by clause 3 of [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. Restricting its objects and morphisms to the full subcategories just proved preserved leaves the equality $T(af)=aT(f)$ intact, and gives the asserted $R$-linear functor.
